Employing bulk Gibbs constructions for both nuclear liquid-gas and hadron-quark phase coexistence, we compute equilibrium configurations across hot neutrino-trapped, hot neutrino-free, and cold stages, alongside linear radial oscillations of selected hot neutrino-free stars. Introducing quarks lowers the maximum baryonic mass at every stage and reverses its evolutionary ordering: whereas the maximum baryonic mass increases toward the cold limit in the purely hadronic model, it decreases progressively in both hybrid models, opening mass windows for delayed collapse. Crucially, despite sharing the same cold limit, PNJL and EPNJL yield distinct baryonic-mass intervals for mixed-core survival across stages: only EPNJL permits configurations that retain mixed cores across both hot stages, whereas only PNJL allows hot neutrino-free mixed-core stars to possess cold equilibrium counterparts. All tested hot neutrino-free mixed-core stars remain linearly stable, yet their fundamental radial frequencies differ substantially. These findings demonstrate that finite-temperature quark dynamics imprints distinct evolutionary constraints and pulsation signatures on proto-neutron stars beyond cold-matter descriptions.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures

papers.t: Discovery of Two Hyperluminous Infrared Galaxies at z~6
papers.abs: Hyperluminous infrared galaxies (HyLIRGs) at cosmic dawn are key to understanding the formation of the first massive galaxies. We report the spectroscopic confirmation of two unlensed HyLIRGs at $z\sim6$ in the COSMOS field, AzTECC63 and S2COS-84, originally selected from single-dish AzTEC and SCUBA-2 surveys. Using ALMA and NOEMA observations, we robustly detected CO and [CII] lines in both galaxies and unambiguously confirmed their redshifts to be $z=6.092$ and $z=5.90$, respectively. Panchromatic SED fitting reveals dust-obscured star formation rates of $\approx1000$ and $\approx2300\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, ranking them among the most intensely star-forming systems known at $z \gtrsim 6$. High-resolution ALMA observations reveal an extremely compact morphology for S2COS-84, with a dust-continuum effective radius of $\approx0.3$ kpc, implying a star-formation rate surface density above the Eddington limit. The far-infrared SEDs of both galaxies, together with the compact size of S2COS-84, indicate warm dust ($T_{\rm dust} \approx 80$ K) that is likely optically thick at far-infrared wavelengths. Both galaxies exhibit an extreme [CII] deficit, with $L_{\rm [C\,II]}/L_{\rm IR} \approx 10^{-3.7}$, an order of magnitude below that of normal star-forming galaxies. Their molecular gas masses, derived consistently from both [C\,{\sc ii}] and dust, together with their IR-derived SFRs imply short gas depletion times of $\approx$40--60 Myr, making them plausible progenitors of the earliest massive quiescent galaxies found at $z\sim5$.
papers.comment: Submitted to A&A

papers.t: Analysis of the Cosmos 2612 - ICEYE-X36 rendezvous and proximity operation from public orbital element data
papers.abs: We analyse the October 2026 close approach between Cosmos 2612 (NORAD 68762) and the commercial radar satellite ICEYE-X36 (NORAD 59103), both in sun-synchronous low Earth orbit, to determine whether it was a rendezvous and proximity operation (RPO) or the result of natural orbital evolution. The public general perturbations (GP) element history from April to October 2026 was propagated with SGP4, and the prediction error was measured empirically for each object. The null hypothesis of natural evolution, tested with manoeuvre-free propagations, is rejected for all 18 parameter combinations: the encounter required manoeuvres by Cosmos 2612, whereas those of ICEYE-X36 are not needed to reproduce it. Closest approach occurred on 18 October at 06:33 UTC, below 0.79 km (95th percentile), with a local relative velocity of about 0.08 m/s and 41.4 h continuously within 5 km. It was the final stage of a sequence that began in May with a plane match, followed by a phasing drift, the approach and a manoeuvred retreat, with a minimum cumulative $Δv$ of 174-180 m/s. The data cannot resolve the minimum distance below their accuracy, nor establish whether the operation was cooperative or its purpose.
papers.comment: 28 pages, 12 figures, 7 tables. Submitted to Acta Astronautica. Code and derived results: https://github.com/bnbuitragom/cosmos2612-iceye-x36-rpo-analysis

papers.t: Survey of Compact Sources for Pulsars and Exotic Objects-II. Precision Timing of Millisecond Pulsar J1840+1102
papers.abs: We present the timing analysis of the eclipsing millisecond pulsar PSR J1840+1102, discovered in the Survey of COmpact sources for Pulsars and Exotic objects (SCOPE) using the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT). PSR J1840+1102 has a short spin period of 1.60 ms and an orbital period of 1.68 days, with a dispersion measure (DM) of 98.8 pc cm$^{-3}$. We report timing analysis over a 2.7-year baseline, yielding a phase-connected solution with a post-fit residual RMS of 2.1 $μ$s. Enabled by the timing solution, we report discovery of pulsed gamma-rays from PSR J1840+1102, with the gamma-ray peak aligned with that of the radio profile. PSR J1840+1102 also exhibits remarkably short eclipses, lasting only around $0.4\%$ of the total orbit at 650 MHz. Based on optical searches, the orbital parameters, short eclipses, and comparison with the known binary pulsar population, we infer a Helium white dwarf (He-WD) surrounded by plasma to be the most likely companion. Furthermore, using GMRT observations covering 300 to 750 MHz, we present a study of the interstellar medium properties towards PSR J1840+1102 including refractive scintillation, DM variations and scattering, and report a very low scattering index of $1.65\pm0.15$. The low timing residuals and lack of any prominent orbital parameters or DM variations support the overall suitability of PSR J1840+1102 for inclusion in the pulsar timing array campaigns.
papers.comment: Submitted to ApJ

papers.t: Modeling the chemical impacts of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes
papers.abs: Some protostars undergo episodic accretion, resulting in luminosity outbursts that heat their envelopes. The increase in temperature alters the position of the snowlines, which return to their original locations on different timescales depending on the species. However, the chemical effects of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes, including their long-term consequences, remain poorly explored. We investigate the chemical impact of luminosity outbursts on the envelope of a solar-type protostar, accounting for its dynamics, and identify trends in the molecular response relative to both ongoing and past outburst activity. We combined the dynamic semi-analytic code APE with the three-phase chemical model NAUTILUS to predict the time evolution of 83 molecular abundances between 10 and 10,000 au in the collapsing envelope. The outburst was parameterized by increasing the protostellar luminosity by a factor of 100 for 100 years. The outburst shifts molecular snowlines outward by up to a factor of ten, thus enriching the gas phase through thermal desorption. Most species return to their pre-outburst state within a few thousand years at most for r$\leq$1000 au and remain in that state thereafter. However, eight molecules (HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, C2H5CHO, OCS, SO2, C2S, C3S, and HC3N) show abundance deviations 10$-$50 kyr after the outburst in the warm inner regions (T$\geq$100 K), due to the inward transport of chemically altered material. Eight other species (CH3O, C2O, NH2, HCCO, HCNO, HNO, NO, and NCO) show enhanced gas-phase abundances at intermediate radii ($\sim$300$-$1500 au). Overall, most molecules are impacted by outward snowline shifts. With the exception of HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, and C2H5CHO, all complex organic molecules (COMs) are expected to exhibit similar abundances in the warm inner regions of protostars (hot corino), regardless of whether they undergo outbursts.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 15 figures, accepted for publication in A&A

papers.t: On extracting Science information from a large data set of RXTE X-ray binary spectra using KDE technique
papers.abs: Machine Learning/Neural Networks have been successively and extensively used in Astronomy (and other subjects) for class identification of objects based on large data sets. However, it remains difficult to extract other science information, such as what the characteristics of the class are that allow for definite identification, and whether there are objects in the sample that are unique and hence of possible science interest. An alternate approach based on rank ordering of variables and Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) may be used for class identification and to infer such science information. We test the method on a previously analyzed data set of RXTE spectra of low-mass X-ray binaries and find that black hole and neutron star systems can be distinguished at an accuracy level of ~93%, which is comparable to deep learning techniques. The soft state spectra of black hole systems are distinct from neutron star ones. For the whole sample, observations of the pulsar 4U 1907+097 (which was inadvertently introduced into the data set) were clearly found to be unique. The previously reported hyper-soft states of GRO J1655-40 and XTE J1550-564 are found to be unique among black hole spectra. For the rest of the neutron stars, the method identifies some unreported spectra of EXO 1745-248 as unique because they seem to be relativistic reflection-dominated spectra. We discuss the potential and scalability of this method.
papers.comment: 9 Pages, 5 figures

papers.t: On the subtleties of statistical isotropy in cosmic topology
papers.abs: The cosmological principle assumes homogeneity and isotropy on the largest scales for which the cosmic microwave background (CMB) provides the best testing grounds. Here, an analysis of the statistical isotropy for the CMB in the case of the cubic 3-torus topology is presented. Since the statistical anisotropy in the CMB 3-torus sky maps is very tiny, the analysis requires very large ensembles consisting of 100000 CMB simulations in order to reveal deviations from the isotropy. Orbit sum rules, which also have applications in quantum chaos, are used to describe the anisotropy structures found in the torus ensembles. They relate the length of orbits, which connect a given point on the surface of last scattering with the topological mirror points of the CMB observer, to the anisotropy pattern. It is found that the positions on the surface of last scattering which are closest to mirror observers possess the largest deviations from the statistical isotropy. Furthermore, the anisotropy of the normalised modulus of the gradient of the CMB temperature field is discussed.

papers.t: Integrated Study of NGC 1662, NGC 1778, NGC 2422, and NGC 2437 Open Clusters: from Stellar Parameters to Orbital Trajectories Utilizing Gaia DR3 Archive
papers.abs: We present a comprehensive photometric, astrometric, and dynamical study of four Galactic open clusters, NGC 1662, NGC 1778, NGC 2422, and NGC 2437, using Gaia DR3 data. Probable cluster members were identified through astrometric and photometric criteria. Radial density profiles were modelled with a King-type surface-density distribution to derive structural parameters. Mean parallaxes and proper motions yielded astrometric distances of 410 +/- 12 pc (NGC 1662), 1761 +/- 335 pc (NGC 1778), 477 +/- 18 pc (NGC 2422), and 1681 +/- 172 pc (NGC 2437). Fundamental astrophysical parameters were estimated through Bayesian isochrone fitting using PARSEC evolutionary models within an MCMC framework. The resulting ages (log(t/yr)) are 8.91 (-0.33/+0.24), 8.20 (-0.11/+0.18), 7.80 (-0.11/+0.06), and 8.56 (-0.34/+0.27), respectively. Luminosity functions were transformed into present-day mass functions using an isochrone-based mass-luminosity relation. The derived mass-function slopes are broadly consistent, within uncertainties, with the classical Salpeter form. Mean systemic radial velocities from Gaia DR3 and complementary spectroscopic surveys enabled the determination of Galactic space velocities (U, V, W) in the Local Standard of Rest frame. Backward orbital integrations over 3 Gyr were performed using galpy with the MWPotential2014 Galactic potential. The resulting orbits are nearly circular (e <= 0.106), with limited vertical excursions (Z_max < 0.3 kpc), consistent with thin-disc kinematics. Inferred birth radii suggest possible outward radial displacement for NGC 2422, NGC 2437, and NGC 1778, and inward displacement for NGC 1662. Overall, all four clusters appear to have evolved within relatively stable Galactic disc orbits.
papers.comment: 25 pages, 16 figures, 7 tables. Accepted for publication in Advances in Space Research

papers.t: Outflows and Young Stars in the Auriga-California Giant Molecular Cloud
papers.abs: The Auriga-California Molecular Cloud (AMC) is a nearby star-forming region with a moderate level of star formation activity. Previous infrared surveys have shown that its young stellar population is concentrated along a dense filament extending north of NGC 1579. We searched for new manifestations of ongoing star formation in the AMC by identifying optical and molecular outflows, Hα emission-line stars, and young stars associated with reflection nebulae. Narrowband Hα and [SII] imaging, together with slitless spectroscopy, were obtained with the 1-m Schmidt telescope of the Byurakan Observatory. The optical data were complemented by near-infrared images from the Spitzer Enhanced Imaging Products (SEIP) and by WISE/unWISE archival data. We discovered seven new Herbig-Haro (HH) objects and outflows associated with several young stellar objects, including deeply embedded infrared sources and stars surrounded by compact reflection nebulae. Nearly all of the optical HH objects have molecular hydrogen counterparts, and several additional candidate H2 outflows without optical counterparts were identified. Particularly noteworthy is a compact region around V347 Per that appears to host at least three molecular outflows. We also present a list of newly identified Hα emission-line stars and a catalogue of stars associated with optical reflection nebulae. Both populations are concentrated primarily along the northern dark filament of the cloud. The spatial distribution of the newly identified HH objects, molecular outflows, emission-line stars, and nebulous young stars confirms that the northern filament is the principal site of ongoing star formation in the AMC. The close correspondence between the optical and molecular outflowsfurther suggests that most of their driving sources are deeply embedded Class 0/I young stellar objects.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 9 figures. To be published in Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics (RAA)

papers.t: Is the learner or the summary the limit? Auditing machine-learning energy reconstruction for air-shower arrays on KASCADE and GRAPES-3
papers.abs: Machine-learning energy estimators for cosmic-ray arrays are usually trained on a few fitted shower parameters, not station signals. When their resolution stops improving, standard diagnostics cannot say whether a better model would help or the summary has run out of information. We use a five-step audit that compares trained models with a learner-independent estimate of the lowest error the summary allows (its squared-loss Bayes risk, or floor), tests which inputs add information and flags inputs merely computed from the fit. We apply it to public KASCADE simulations with three hadronic-interaction models (QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC and SIBYLL-2.3d), to 13,848,509 measured KASCADE events and to simulated GRAPES-3 events. Within known energy decades below 10^16 eV, gradient boosting on nine reconstructed features is within 2.2% of the estimated floor under every estimator setting, so more capacity is not expected to gain more than about 2%. The floor is an estimate, accurate to about 1% in a semi-synthetic benchmark with intervals that under-cover, and not a bound on the true Bayes risk. Replacing reconstructed by true particle numbers removes 70 to 72% of the error variance below 10^15 eV and 24 to 26% between 10^16 and 10^17 eV on all three models, yet simulated station signals close about a tenth of that gap. On GRAPES-3, networks given images rendered from the fit do no better than the fit. In measured data, the mean muon size at fixed electron size lies within every model's proton-to-iron bracket and a label-free probe finds the muon channel used as in simulation; neither fixes the energy scale. Energy-labelled results are simulated.
papers.comment: 26 pages, 14 figures, 14 tables. Submitted to Eur. Phys. J. C. Code: https://github.com/SamarjeetMalik/summary-representation-limits

papers.t: A novel mechanism for coherent radio emission: particle-in-cell simulations
papers.abs: It has been established that electron (phase-space) holes, i.e., EHs, can arise from the nonlinear relaxation of the electron beam instability. Excitation of electromagnetic waves related to the EHs is, however, still not fully understood. Using 2.5-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations, we systematically investigate the nonlinear evolution of the (moderately relativistic) electron bi-stream instability (a special case of the electron beam instability where the densities of the two counter-propagating energetic electron beams are equivalent) in charge- and current-neutralized plasmas under weak and strong magnetizations. This study provides new insights into the wave excitation, the nonlinear wave-particle interactions, the formation of non-Maxwellian features, and the anisotropic electron heating in magnetized plasmas, with potential implications for coherent radio emission in astrophysical plasmas (e.g., solar zebra-pattern bursts).

papers.t: Asteroseismic investigation of intermediate age open star cluster NGC 2126
papers.abs: We present a preliminary asteroseismic investigation of the pulsating stars in the intermediate-age open cluster NGC 2126. The TESS Full Frame Images and ground-based photometry from the previous study, Dileep et al. (2025), were used to identify the pulsation modes of δ Scuti member stars using period-luminosity relations and pulsation modelling. Our analysis resulted in a tentative identification up to the first radial overtone in stars N1, N2 and ZV1. Additionally, the second radial overtone was secured in N1. The disentangled pulsation and eclipse light curves of the binary star V551 Aur (V6) from our previous research were employed to study pulsation amplitude and phase modulations across the orbital period. The primary component of V6 exhibits pulsations showing amplitude and phase modulations, indicating tidal influence on the oscillations. Modelling the pulsation as the fundamental radial mode reveals that in order for the mode to be radial, the star must be significantly brighter than observed. Hence, the mode is not the fundamental radial mode or the overtones. Low-resolution spectroscopy was used to search for chemical peculiarities in the pulsating members, and we found that star ID 143 has features similar to an Am star.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in proceedings of the 4th BINA workshop (07 July 2026), held on 4th-7th November 2025 at the University of Calicut, India

papers.t: Insights on Three Distinct Types of Energetic Particle Flux Variations Ahead of ICME-driven Shocks Observed by ASPEX on board Aditya-L1
papers.abs: We investigate upstream energetic-ion transport associated with ten interplanetary coronal mass ejection (ICME)-driven shocks observed near 1 au using multidirectional measurements from the Suprathermal and Energetic Particle Spectrometer (STEPS) onboard Aditya-L1. Based on energy-dependent intensity profiles and onset times, the events are classified as dispersed, dispersionless, or mixed. We combine pitch-angle anisotropy, minimum variance analysis, reduced magnetic helicity, two-dimensional Grad-Shafranov reconstruction, quasi-linear transport diagnostics, shock parameters, and energetic-ion spectral fits to characterize each category. The seven dispersed events exhibit energy-dependent arrivals, generally intermittent magnetic-helicity signatures, and larger parallel mean free paths, consistent with less restricted particle propagation. In contrast, the two dispersionless events show nearly simultaneous enhancements across energy channels, extended intervals of enhanced reduced magnetic helicity, and closed magnetic flux contours in Grad-Shafranov reconstructions. They also exhibit shorter parallel mean free paths, higher pitch-angle diffusion coefficients, and comparatively strong shocks. The mixed event transitions from dispersed arrivals to nearly simultaneous enhancements as the shock approaches, accompanied by evolving anisotropy and distinct scattering properties. Spectral indices range from approximately -2.38 to -0.86 for dispersed events and from -0.82 to -0.26 for dispersionless and mixed events, indicating harder spectra in the latter groups. These results reveal systematic associations between energetic-ion transport, magnetic structure, shock conditions, and spectral hardness, suggesting that shock-associated energization and energy-dependent transport jointly shape the observed signatures, while magnetic topology may regulate particle propagation and confinement.
papers.comment: Accepted in The Astrophysical Journal Letters (ApJL), 34 Pages, 9 Figures, and 3 Tables

papers.t: Constraining Dehnen-inspired dark matter halo with S2 star's orbit
papers.abs: We use the orbit of S2 star around Sagittarius A* to constrain three black hole backgrounds motivated by Dehnen profiles with inner slopes $γ=0$, $1$, and $5/2$, which are characterized by the scale radius $r_s$ and density $ρ_s$ of the dark matter halo. An exact turning-point integral gives the pericenter advance at finite eccentricity, and an exterior expansion identifies the leading halo contributions. A fifteen-parameter Bayesian analysis combines astrometric and spectroscopic observations with the measured precession parameter, from which we obtain the marginalized $1σ$ upper limits $r_s/M<0.236$, $0.168$, and $0.030$, and $ρ_sM^2<0.536$, $0.578$, and $0.004$, respectively. The leading halo monopole in the first two metrics is degenerate with the central mass. At fixed dynamical mass, their leading radial profile correction produces retrograde precession. The $γ=5/2$ metric introduces an additional angular deficit contribution, which enhances the precession response and accounts for its smaller parameter limits.
papers.comment: 18pages

papers.t: Quantifying the Impact of Galactic Dark Matter Halo Models on LZ Results
papers.abs: Most dark matter direct-detection limits are reported under the assumption of an isotropic, Maxwellian Standard Halo Model. However, the Milky Way's stellar halo exhibits substantial radial anisotropy, while cosmological simulations predict scale-dependent anisotropy in the dark matter velocity distribution. We investigate how departures from isotropy affect the interpretation of LZ results in two complementary regimes: background-dominated elastic-scattering searches and the recently reported 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate, which we study using a background-free single-event approximation. For elastic scattering, we use the self-consistent isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt, axisymmetric, and triaxial halo models of Belli et al. and translate the published limits through the ratio of predicted event counts, applying a common escape-speed truncation in the Galactic frame. At WIMP masses above approximately 40 GeV, the resulting limits lie within about $\pm 30\%$ of the isotropic reference. Below approximately 15 GeV, the model envelope broadens to as much as an order of magnitude, reflecting sensitivity to the high-velocity tail. For the 248 keV event, the accessible inelastic mass splitting is likewise controlled by this tail. Some anisotropic models extend the allowed kinematic region towards splittings at which solar-neutrino constraints on a Higgsino interpretation become ineffective, although kinematic accessibility alone does not establish viability at the fixed Higgsino cross section. These results show that halo-model dependence is modest at high WIMP masses but becomes essential near kinematic thresholds.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures

papers.t: Sound of Keplerian binaries in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background
papers.abs: We formulate the dissipation due to sound-wave emission from a Keplerian binary embedded in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background at rest in the binary center-of-mass frame within linear perturbation theory. Rather than starting from the local wake force, we treat the binary as a localized periodic mass source and compute the sound-wave fluxes carried away by the medium. The time-averaged energy, linear-momentum, and angular-momentum fluxes are obtained from Noether currents of the fluid perturbations. For a classical inviscid barotropic Newtonian fluid, retaining the self-gravity of density perturbations while adopting the Jeans prescription, we derive explicit flux formulas for circular and eccentric binaries with arbitrary mass ratio. This formulation also clarifies the ultraviolet behavior of point sources: in a nondispersive fluid, the harmonic sum becomes cutoff-sensitive precisely when at least one component becomes supersonic. We examine explicitly how finite source size removes this divergence using a uniform-sphere model and relate the resulting regularization to a corresponding effective harmonic cutoff. The associated secular eccentricity evolution exhibits circularization in the subsonic regime when the fluid self-gravity is sufficiently weak but can change sign outside this regime, with eccentricity growth in the strictly supersonic UV limit. For a Schrödinger-Poisson quantum fluid, quantum pressure instead softens the high-frequency contribution and renders the point-source fluxes UV finite within the nonrelativistic regime; our numerical results further indicate eccentricity growth due to sound radiation over the parameter space explored. Finally, we translate orbital-decay measurements of two binary pulsars into order-of-magnitude bounds on the homogeneous quantum-fluid density surrounding each system.
papers.comment: 26 pages, 9 figures; published version

papers.t: Identifying Distant and Highly Reddened Star Clusters: 486 Open Clusters and Candidates in the Dusty Galactic Disk
papers.abs: The Gaia mission has transformed the census of Galactic star clusters. Most discoveries were based on Gaia DR2 and EDR3, and the rate of new large cluster catalogues has declined since 2023. The distant and dusty part of the disk is still poorly sampled because optical data are strongly affected by extinction. We search for star clusters in the Galactic disk using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry, together with 2MASS near-infrared photometry. We scan trial cluster centers in Galactic position, proper motion, and parallax space, assign a Bayesian membership probability to each star, construct a relative density map, and use DBSCAN solely to separate neighboring peaks. We identify 486 clusters and candidates with astrometric quality comparable to that of previously reported clusters. Of these, 450 have no literature counterpart, while 36 are known clusters that were not recovered in earlier Gaia cluster searches. The median distance is 6.9 kpc, and 39% of the objects lie beyond 8 kpc. The median extinction is Av = 5.10 mag, and 16% of the objects have Av > 8mag. The new objects fill a sparsely sampled region of the distance--extinction plane. Their distribution reveals the north--south displacement of the Galactic warp, and high-latitude objects are on average farther, older, and less extincted. Gaia DR3 still offers room for distant, dust-obscured clusters, and this sample provides a baseline for Gaia DR4. All cluster parameters, member star information, spatial distribution maps, and color-magnitude diagrams can be downloaded from https://zenodo.org/records/24431850.
papers.comment: The 486 new cluster data can be downloaded from https://zenodo.org/records/24431850

papers.t: Scale-dependent Dark Matter in a Multi-component Cosmological Framework: Distinct Components Governing Galactic and Cosmological Dynamics
papers.abs: In this work we generalize the concept of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter from galactic to cosmological scales. At galactic scales, the scale-dependent equation of state which successfully describes dark matter dominated galaxies has a nearly isothermal equation of state of the form $P(r)=K(r)ρ(r)$, where the entropy function $K(r)$ is radius dependent and slowly varying with the galactic radius. Using appropriate theoretical arguments, the successful galactic scale dark matter model is generalized to have a universal equation of state of the form $\langle P(χ)\rangle =\langle ρ(χ)\rangle \langle σ_{DM}^2\rangle$, where $χ$ is the scale of the system under study and it can describe cosmological or galactic scales and $σ_{DM}$ is the characteristic velocity dispersion of dark matter at the relevant scales. This results to the entropy function behaving universally as $K(χ)=\langle σ_{DM}^2\rangle$. We investigate the cosmological implications of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter, and we conclude that this scale-dependent equation of state dark matter cannot be the sole component of dark matter in the Universe. Also the second aim of this work is to provide a sufficient explanation for the question why $K_0$ changes for each galaxy, where $K_0$ is the value of $K(r)$ at intermediate and large radii from the core of the galaxy. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of having distinct dark matter components which cluster differently, and thus controlling differently the dynamics of the Universe at various scales. Scale-dependent equation of state dark matter can control the galactic scales, while another component can dominate at cosmological scales and thus control the Universe at cosmological scales.

papers.t: Finite-Temperature Stabilization of a KKLT Modulus in Three-Dimensional Lattice Simulations
papers.abs: We investigate the cosmological stabilization of a KKLT modulus through three-dimensional Langevin lattice simulations incorporating an evolving thermal bath, dissipation, spatial gradients, and stochastic fluctuations. While the spatially averaged modulus closely follows homogeneous evolution away from the capture threshold, near-critical trajectories linger near the unstable potential barrier for approximately one e-fold, allowing long-wavelength fluctuations to undergo tachyonic amplification and drive localized regions across the barrier even as the mean field turns back toward the stabilized vacuum. Linear Langevin theory reproduces the fluctuation growth, while convergence tests identify a narrow stochastic layer in which the barrier-crossing fraction shows no systematic dependence on the discretization at a fixed effective distance from the threshold. These results demonstrate that capture of the spatially averaged modulus does not guarantee that every spatial region remains within the stabilizing barrier.

papers.t: Probabilistic Inversion of Strong Gravitational Lenses with Flow Matching Priors
papers.abs: Strong gravitational lensing reveals important information about the universe, but reconstructing the source image and lens properties requires solving an ill-posed inverse imaging problem. Generative image models serve as powerful data-driven priors in Bayesian inverse problems. Diffusion models have been used widely, but they are computationally costly. Flow matching has emerged as a promising alternative to diffusion models, with easier training, efficient sampling, and better-quality data generation. In this work, we present Blind-FlowSGS, a principled blind posterior sampling method using flow matching priors, enabling efficient posterior sampling for non-blind and blind inversion of strong gravitational lenses. On simulated Euclid data, we demonstrate our method's improvement over diffusion-based methods in both efficacy and efficiency. Our method shows promising capabilities to accurately process strong lensing data from modern sky surveys at scale. Our code and data are available on our project page.
papers.comment: Accepted to the 9th Annual Workshop for Machine Learning & the Physical Sciences (ML4PS), 2026

papers.t: Validating Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations with Close Visual Binaries
papers.abs: We validate a subset of the astrometric accelerations reported in Gaia DR3 non-single-star solutions by their consistency with the gravitational pull of known, resolved companions. Cross-matching 338,215 DR3 acceleration solutions against the Washington Double Star (WDS) catalog of visual binaries yields 2,466 unique pairs within 2". For each pair we compare the measured acceleration with alpha_max, the Newtonian bound on the acceleration the companion can impart on the Gaia-tracked photocenter. For 98.1% of the pairs the measured acceleration exceeds this bound by more than a factor of 10, so the cataloged companion cannot be responsible and the perturber must be a closer, unresolved one. The remaining 45 plausible wide binaries are close pairs at the WDS resolution limit. We fit orbits with an updated orvara, extended to accept the DR3 acceleration and jerk coefficients as direct constraints and released with htof as part of this work. The fits converge for 16 of the 45 and one boundary case, the rest having too few resolved measures or a perturber other than the cataloged pair, and 13 of the 17 carry enough data to test the coefficients. Eleven of the 13 statistically accommodate the reported accelerations, for seven- and nine-parameter solutions alike, and the dynamical companion masses agree with the photometric estimates where the photocenter conversion is well determined. Independently of the fits, 33 of the 43 plausible systems with a usable position angle (77%) have the acceleration directed within 45 degrees of the primary-companion axis, against 50% for a control sample: DR3's measured accelerations point in the directions of the cataloged companions.
papers.comment: 26 pages, 8 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to AJ

papers.t: DIPS-OjOS I: Project Design and Science Validation
papers.abs: Automated pipelines and machine-learning algorithms are efficient at detecting standard planetary transits, but can miss subtle, non-periodic morphological anomalies. We present the pilot phase of DIPS-OjOS (Detecting Irregular Photometric Signals - OjímetrO Survey), a professional-amateur collaboration designed to develop and validate a scalable workflow for identifying irregular photometric signals in exoplanet transit light curves through trained visual inspection. The project targets starspot-crossing events, stellar flares, circumplanetary structures, exomoon-like signatures, and transit-duration or timing anomalies overlooked by automated searches. We built the infrastructure required for a controlled visual-inspection experiment: simulated control light curves, preparation and detrending of real short-cadence Kepler data, a transit-modeling pipeline that computes an optimized average transit profile for each light curve, and a web-based classification platform. The real sample was deliberately restricted to 51 well-characterized Kepler systems. Collaborators inspected 917 transit events: 555 real transits and 362 simulated controls. The simulated sample quantified observer performance and calibrated a weighted consensus scheme; collaborators recovered injected signals with an average efficiency of 87.6%, while the null-case false-positive rate was 15.3%. After expert validation, we retained 88 viable candidate anomalies from the real sample, including 26 starspot-crossing event candidates across eight targets, seven stellar flares, 31 systematic transit-duration deviations motivating refined orbital parameters in four systems, and a mutual transit event in Kepler-89. Recovering candidate signals in this well-studied sample validates the sensitivity of DIPS-OjOS and establishes the basis for future applications to Kepler, TESS, PLATO, and ground-based datasets.
papers.comment: 18 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Accepted for publication in PASP. This is the version originally submitted to the journal, before peer review

papers.t: Refined, Reliable and Reproducible: Algorithmic Analysis and Reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder
papers.abs: Cosmic voids are vast underdense regions of the Universe that encode valuable information about its large-scale structure and evolution. By extending spherical voids into overlapping sphere structures, the Popcorn Void Finder demonstrated an improved statistical characterization of cosmic void populations. However, its origin as a research prototype progressively hindered its maintainability and extensibility. Moreover, post-publication algorithmic modifications have not been systematically evaluated, leaving their statistical and computational consequences insufficiently characterized. In this work, we present a comprehensive reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder, prioritizing algorithmic transparency, maintainability, and reproducibility. We document the complete identification procedure, revisit the original algorithmic choices, and evaluate their statistical and computational consequences. Comparisons between implementations revealed a significant change in the behavior of the Void Size Function, which is now characterized by a power-law regime transitioning to a Schechter-like distribution. These changes not only provide a better characterization of void sizes, but enable a new and more robust method to the determination of the shot-noise dominated regime, without implicit dependencies on internal finder parameters present in previous works. Performance benchmarks demonstrate a 1.62x speedup in spherical void identification and a substantial improvement in overlap-removal throughput. We determined the Popcorn algorithm to be negatively affected by load imbalance, and found a speedup of 63x in a tested configuration with a newly introduced early growth termination criterion. These results establish a more maintainable and reproducible foundation for popcorn void identification, while clarifying the statistical and computational trade-offs that govern its performance.

papers.t: Evaluating VLT SPHERE for Probing Diffuse Circumstellar Regions of Evolved Stars
papers.abs: Red and Yellow Supergiant stars, generally found in late evolutionary stages with high mass loss, provide test cases for evaluating high-contrast imaging performance. Determining how well adaptive optics combined with coronagraphy isolates faint circumstellar emission allows us to define its true sensitivity limits for evolved stars and refine future high-contrast observing strategies. We conducted a pilot study of seven nearby (within 0.8 kpc), bright (V-band magnitude of 10 or less) evolved red and yellow supergiants. We selected these targets to evaluate the ability of the VLT's SPHERE/IRDIS high-contrast imaging instrument to detect faint, diffuse circumstellar emission in four infrared filters (J1, J2, K1, and K2). We processed the data using RDI to remove the stellar PSF, AO speckles, and diffraction patterns. We extracted radial profiles and performed Radon transform analysis to search for faint extended emission around each target. We detect no extended circumstellar emission in our high-contrast images or clear infrared excess in the SEDs of our seven targets. Injection-recovery tests demonstrate sensitivity to diffuse emission at contrasts of approximately 3.5 mag in the J1 and approximately 2.0 mag in K1 relative to the residual coronagraphic PSF halo. This study provides the first results that elucidate the observational conditions under which SPHERE/IRDIS fails to recover low surface brightness emission and highlights the observational factors that most strongly control detectability, including filter choice, sky calibration, and reference-star matching. Our results motivate future studies to prioritize targets with infrared excess and optimize observing strategies to improve sensitivity to faint circumstellar emission around evolved massive stars.
papers.comment: 17 pages, accepted for publication in The Astronomical Journal

papers.t: Reassessment of Planetary Parameters and Statistical Validation of 187 Kepler Habitable-Zone and Near Habitable Confirmed and Candidate Planets
papers.abs: Confirmed and candidate planets in the Habitable or near-Habitable Zones (HZ) orbiting Sun-like stars are crucial not only for the search for life beyond the Solar System, but also for understanding the architecture and formation of other solar systems and for conducting demographic studies. Current analyses of such planetary systems are limited both by the small sample size revealed by Kepler as well as by uncertainties in system parameters. Although a larger sample of HZ and near-HZ planets must await new observations from wide-field, space-based surveys, follow-up analyses and observations with existing facilities can improve the precision on stellar and planetary parameters, enable more accurate planetary classification, and a more reliable assessment of whether candidate systems are true planets or merely astrophysical false positives. Here, we present a homogeneous transit light curve analysis of 187 HZ and near-HZ systems discovered by Kepler. Our analysis incorporates the latest Gaia DR3-derived stellar parameters, and we also present a statistical validation effort for all targets. The result is a uniform set of planetary radii, instellation fluxes, and orbital ephemerides suitable for prioritizing and scheduling follow-up observations to improve our understanding of planets in this regime. We show that longer-period (>300days) systems would particularly benefit from transit follow-up: just a single transit from facilities such as the 6m James Webb or the planned 3m Lazuli space telescopes could provide ~2 times tighter precision on planet radii than four years of Kepler photometry, thereby dramatically shrinking relevant parameter uncertainties and allowing more confident planet/false-positive assessments.
papers.comment: Accepted to AJ on 13th November 2026

papers.t: Neural-Network Approximators for Low-Thrust Multi-Asteroid Rendezvous Optimization
papers.abs: Designing low-thrust multi-asteroid rendezvous missions requires the coupled selection of asteroid sequences, encounter epochs, and low-thrust trajectories. Lambert transfers support rapid beam search but do not directly describe thrust-limited transfer capacity or propellant consumption. This paper develops two complementary low-thrust neural approximators. The first directly predicts the continuous maximum admissible initial mass from numerically optimized low-thrust transfers, providing a transfer-capacity estimate for comparison with the current spacecraft mass. The second predicts mass-dependent propellant consumption and propagates spacecraft mass to subsequent legs. With the carefully-designed input features and network structure, the approximators reduce mean absolute errors by 72.2% and 75.5%, respectively, relative to conventional deep neural network baselines. These predictions are incorporated into a Lambert-ranked beam search through resource filtering and recursive mass propagation before final beam selection. The method is evaluated on fixed-visit, maximum-visit, and deployment-collection missions. Across the tested cases, the proposed resource filtering increases the fraction of candidate sequences that yield accepted low-thrust solutions, raises the maximum validated asteroid-visit count by up to 15.4%, and improves the best mission objective by up to 17.8%. These results demonstrate that continuous transfer-capacity and propellant predictions can improve finite-width sequence search.

papers.t: Wavelet-CFM for the extragalactic millimeter-wave sky
papers.abs: We develop a Wavelet-factorized Conditional Flow Matching (Wavelet-CFM) framework to generate fast, accurate simulations of correlated astrophysical fields including gravitational lensing convergence ($κ$), the kinetic and thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ and tSZ) effects, and cosmic infrared background (CIB) emission. Together these make up every bright extragalactic component of the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) sky apart from radio sources. Our approach combines multi-scale wavelet decomposition with conditional flow matching models, trained on $\sim$9$\times$9 deg$^2$ patches at 1-arcminute resolution. The four fields are generated jointly, including their cross couplings, and the model has a tractable likelihood, which to our knowledge has not previously been achieved for this set of components. The power spectra, one-point distributions and Minkowski functionals of the generated maps match a validation set to a few percent. These results show promise for enabling field-level cosmological analyses of mm-wave data.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Accepted to the 9th Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences Workshop (ML4PS)

papers.t: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems
papers.abs: Most stars in the field are part of binary, triple, or higher-order systems, which we primarily observe in hierarchical configurations that allow long-term stability. Over long timescales, hierarchical triple systems interact primarily through gravitational dynamics, but more complex interactions arise when stellar evolution drives mass transfer. In this paper, we study tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We find that the finite separation of the inner binary produces oscillations in the Roche potential that critically alter both the donor star's variability and its mean mass-loss rate. For compact inner binaries, the mass-loss rate approaches that of a single accretor, while at larger separations the orbit-averaged mass-loss rate increases steeply, approximately as $\langle \dot{M}_d\rangle \propto \langle \dot{M}_{d,0}\rangle (1+C a_b^{6.1 \pm 0.9})$. For the $γ= 5/3$ polytropic donor considered here, this scaling is consistent with the nonlinear response of Roche-lobe overflow to the leading quadrupolar perturbation of the inner-binary potential, which scales as $δΦ_2 \propto a_b^2$. We also examine the donor's response to periodic forcing from the inner binary and find a transition between individual and collaborative accretion that determines whether the transferred material can form and sustain a circumbinary disk. Our results show that the finite separation of the inner binary can strongly regulate both the rate and fate of tertiary mass transfer, constraining a poorly understood phase of hierarchical triple evolution.

papers.t: Chemical structure of the solar neighbourhood with DESI DR1
papers.abs: We analyse the chemical, spatial, and kinematic properties of stars in the solar neighbourhood using DESI Data Release 1 combined with Gaia astrometry. A high-quality FGK dwarf sample is separated into low-$α$ and high-$α$ populations using Gaussian mixture modelling in the [$α$/Fe]--[Fe/H] plane. The low-$α$ population is more metal rich, dominates near the Galactic mid-plane, and shows negative radial and vertical metallicity gradients. The high-$α$ population is more metal poor, has a steeper vertical metallicity gradient, an approximately flat radial metallicity profile, and dynamically hotter kinematics. Despite these differences, the two chemically defined populations overlap substantially in velocity space. These results indicate distinct chemical enrichment histories for the low-$α$ and high-$α$ populations, while showing that chemical classification does not map uniquely onto present-day kinematic components. The observed chemo-dynamical structure is consistent with the combined effects of chemical enrichment, radial redistribution, and secular dynamical evolution in shaping the Galactic disc.
papers.comment: 13 pages. Published in Astronomy & Astrophysics

papers.t: Constraining Planet Nine with Pulsar Timing: Orbit Determination Method from the Acceleration, Jerk, and Snap of the Solar System Barycenter
papers.abs: Planet Nine is hypothesized to exist in the outer solar system in order to explain the physical orbital clustering of several trans-Neptunian objects. A Planet Nine would systematically change the location of the solar system barycenter (SSB). Therefore, the precise timing properties of millisecond radio pulsars would measure the acceleration, jerk, and snap of the currently-perceived SSB under the gravitational influence of a Planet Nine. We present a method on how to use pulsar spin frequency derivatives and binary pulsar orbital period derivatives to constrain the Planet Nine parameter space. We find that searches for unidentified massive objects in the solar system require at least cubic and quartic variations in the pulse times of arrival (corresponding to jerk and snap, respectively) in order to uniquely constrain an orbit. Otherwise, additional assumptions are required to fully constrain the mass and orbital parameters of the object. We use our method to weigh the ice giants Uranus and Neptune and obtain results consistent with the literature. This method could be used to weigh a Planet Nine after a putative optical detection. Future work will use updated pulsar timing datasets that benefit from longer observational baselines and advances in statistical modeling and noise characterization.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 1 table; submitted to ApJ

papers.t: Scalar dynamics in a subclass Ia mimetic DHOST bounce
papers.abs: We study scalar perturbations in a quadratic subclass Ia degenerate higher-order scalar-tensor (DHOST) realization of a nonsingular bouncing cosmology previously analyzed in higher-derivative mimetic gravity. After a constant rescaling of the scalar potential, the subclass Ia model reproduces the same scale-factor history as the original model, although the associated mimetic Lagrange multiplier generally differs. For the comparison with the original mimetic model, we focus on the branch $0<γ<2/3$, for which the scalar sound speed of the original model is positive. We perform an ADM and Hamiltonian reduction of the scalar sector and show that, imposing the mimetic and momentum constraints, the reduced canonical scalar mode contains no spatial-gradient contribution. The physical scalar sound speed therefore vanishes, $c_s^2=0$, in agreement with the known vacuum behavior of the \(α_L=0\) mimetic-DHOST sector. On the matched bouncing background, the resulting effective frequency squared is independent of the comoving wavenumber and approaches zero from below in the remote contracting phase. Consequently, the asymptotic oscillatory regime used in the previous mimetic model to impose positive-frequency initial conditions is absent. Although canonical normalization can still be imposed through the Wronskian condition, it does not select the initial state uniquely. Without an additional state prescription, the asymptotic dynamics therefore does not uniquely determine the primordial scalar spectrum.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 2 figures

papers.t: Age dependence of the radial metallicity gradient in the Galactic disc with LAMOST and Gaia
papers.abs: We investigate the stellar radial metallicity ([Fe/H]) gradient--age relation (MGAR) of the Galactic disc using a solar-neighbourhood sample of 580\,037 F-, G-, and K-type (FGK) dwarf and turn-off stars from LAMOST DR7, Gaia Data Release3, and the corrected StarHorse age catalogue. The fiducial MGAR is non-monotonic, with relatively strong negative gradients at intermediate ages followed by substantial flattening towards older populations. The most negative gradient occurs at $6$--$8$ Gyr in the adopted 2-Gyr bins, although the $4$--$6$ Gyr slope is statistically similar, indicating a broad intermediate-age turnover rather than a sharply defined transition. The flattening persists within the low-$α$ population, indicating that chemical-population mixing alone cannot explain the full-sample relation, and is also recovered under alternative guiding-radius definitions, radial fitting ranges, vertical-orbit selections, propagation of the reported random age uncertainties, and an alternative stellar-age scale. In contrast, controlling the age-dependent $T_{\rm eff}$--$\log g$ distribution substantially reduces the absolute gradient amplitudes and modifies the younger-age behaviour. A same-star comparison with APOGEE DR17 further shows that the broad age dependence of the controlled MGAR is recovered using an external [Fe/H] scale. We therefore identify the intermediate-to-old-age flattening as the most robust feature of the observed MGAR, whereas the precise location and depth of the intermediate-age minimum and the detailed younger-age morphology are less stable. These results indicate that stellar-parameter selection can contribute to the diversity of MGAR morphologies reported in previous studies.
papers.comment: 19 pages. Published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
papers.jref: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 553, stag2006 (2026)

papers.t: The Most X-ray Luminous Fast Blue Optical Transient at Early Times: AT 2024qfm and Inefficient Reprocessing of Its High-Energy Emission
papers.abs: We present comprehensive multiwavelength (X-ray, UV, optical, and radio) observations of the Luminous Fast Blue Optical Transient (LFBOT) AT 2024qfm. At $z = 0.227$ and reaching $L_{\rm x}\approx 10^{44}\,\rm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, AT 2024qfm is the most X-ray luminous LFBOT at $δt 10000$ K until $δt \approx 14$ days. AT 2024qfm shows luminous radio emission that is broadly consistent with the interaction of a fast ($Γβc \approx 0.2$ c) shock wave with a dense medium ($n_{\rm CSM} \approx 6 \times 10^{4}\, \rm cm^{-3}$ at $R \approx 1.3 \times 10^{16}$ cm). Interestingly, the radio spectra do not evolve between $δt \approx 40-58$ days, indicating multiple outflow components shocking the surrounding medium. Peculiar to AT2024qfm is that this LFBOT reaches $L_{\rm x} \approx L_{\rm opt}$ at much earlier times ($δt \approx 7$ days) than observed for AT 2018cow and AT 2024wpp, suggesting less efficient re-processing of X-rays. Finally, a compilation of the X-ray spectral properties of all known LFBOTs shows that they consistently exhibit harder X-ray spectra than GRB afterglows, indicating a different emission mechanism and/or regimes between the two source classes.
papers.comment: 28 pages, 12 figures, submitted to ApJ

papers.t: The JWST Resolved Stellar Populations Early Release Science Program. X. Cross-Observatory Proper Motion Measurements with HST and JWST
papers.abs: We present the first absolute systemic proper motion (PM) of a galaxy measured by combining Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and JWST imaging. The PM of WLM, an isolated dwarf galaxy at $\sim$1 Mpc, is measured against background galaxies with Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS) F814W imaging from 2015 and 2024 and NIRCam imaging from 2022 and 2024. The two ACS epochs give a systemic PM of $(μ_α^*, μ_δ) = (+0.087 \pm 0.019, -0.079 \pm 0.017)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 145 galaxies over 8.93 years, which agrees with previous Gaia-based PMs to within 0.4$σ$ and is the most precise PM of WLM. For the HST-to-JWST PMs, we fit each NIRCam detector separately, match the point-spread functions with empirically derived convolution kernels, and correct biases with injected galaxies. With an F090W second epoch, the PM is $(+0.081 \pm 0.045, -0.113 \pm 0.046)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 43 galaxies over 7.02 years, which, like the F150W PM, agrees with HST-to-HST over the same area to within 1$σ$, while F200W differs by $\sim$2$σ$. The long-wavelength F250M and F430M PMs are consistent to within 1$σ$, though less precise. Fewer galaxies can be used at wavelengths farther from F814W. A cross-observatory systematic of $\sim$0.05 mas yr$^{-1}$ cannot be ruled out over 7 years. At equal baselines, an F090W second epoch is at least as precise as our second ACS epoch over the same area. We recommend the NIRCam filter closest in wavelength to the first-epoch filter, though the long-wavelength filters show promise for closer targets or longer baselines.
papers.comment: Submitted to ApJ. 31 pages, 12 figures, 4 tables

papers.t: Modeling extraordinary relativistic jets on the scale of the cosmic web
papers.abs: Recent observations of supermassive black hole jets extending up to the typical sizes of cosmic web filaments challenge our current understanding. In particular, the overall jet size of J152932.16+601534.4 ("Porphyrion") reaches $\sim 7$ Mpc at redshift 0.896. Magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) models of relativistic jets have never been successfully applied to such extraordinary distances, requiring demanding jet-environment and flow stability conditions. By using state-of-the-art numerical simulations of 3D relativistic-MHD jets, we show that Porphyrion's observational properties can be successfully modelled in a realistic scenario, involving a jet kinetic power of $3.5 \times 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and an external medium of a low-density galaxy group. We find that the pair of jets expands to $\sim 9$ Mpc in about $20$ Myr, implying that the jet grows with relativistic speeds for most of its evolution. Comparing this case with other jets of similar power propagating in substantially denser cosmic structures, we find much slower outflows that can only reach a few Mpc, consistent with the bulk of the observed population of giant radio galaxies. Our results make a testable prediction, i.e. future detections of even larger-scale jets in upcoming surveys and database searches will be invaluable in studying the demographics and feedback of the poorly known population of powerful jets, particularly in under-dense regions of the cosmic web.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series

papers.t: Multiplicity of Normal A-Type Field Stars of Low Projected Rotational Velocity
papers.abs: While nearly all rapidly rotating (vsini > 120 km/s) A stars are observed to have normal spectra, a significant fraction (~43%) of slow rotators have peculiar spectra although many do not. For over 30 years, we conducted a radial velocity survey of 119 non-peculiar, slowly rotating dwarf or subgiant A stars. We determined orbital elements and related parameters for 43 systems and along with known visual binaries, common proper motion companions and stars with proper motion anomalies, find a multiplicity fraction of 0.64. We compared our results to recent findings concerning similar stars. We also examined whether the slow rotation of our sample of could have been caused by tidal interactions in short-period binaries. Of the 80 stars that we determined to be at least binary in nature or to show other evidence of having companions, only 6 have periods < 10 days. Thus, a large majority have periods that are much too long for tidal forces to have reduced their rotation rates while they are on the main-sequence. We also observed a small sample of rapid rotators (vsini = 125-230 km/s) over a shorter time interval to judge the accuracy of our measuring techniques on A stars with very broad lines. Orbital elements for 5 non-survey A-type stars, also with low vsini, are listed with our results, but are not included in the statistical discussion.
papers.comment: 51 pages, 12 figures, 12 tables, 2 appendices. Submitted to AAS Journals

papers.t: The FRB Population Revisited: Rate, Energy, Evolution, and Host-DM Constraints from the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog
papers.abs: We present a study that simultaneously fits for key fast radio burst (FRB) population properties using the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog while calibrating for instrumental selection effects. Our inferred volumetric rate at $z=0$ is $1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.3}\times 10^{5}\,{\rm Gpc}^{-3}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ above an isotropic-equivalent energy of $10^{39}$ erg and below a scattering timescale of 30 ms at 600 MHz. The evolution of the FRB rate relative to the cosmic star formation rate remains statistically unconstrained. Assuming a Schechter function for the energy distribution, isotropic emission, and 1-GHz emission bandwidth, we find a characteristic maximum energy of $2.0^{+2.6}_{-1.0} \times 10^{41}$ erg and a differential power-law index of $-1.41\,^{+0.27}_{-0.21}({\rm stat.})\,\pm\,0.35({\rm sys.})$. The host galaxy contribution to the observed dispersion measure (DM) is modeled as a log-normal distribution; assuming a total Galactic contribution of 80 $\text{pc cm}^{-3}$, we find a median host-galaxy DM contribution of $199^{+34}_{-36}\;\text{pc cm}^{-3}$ in the rest-frame. Finally, we find that the average FRB spectrum, described by a spectral index of $α=-1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.6}$, is inconsistent with being flat at the $\sim2σ$ level. We note an excess of high-S/N bursts at low DMs in the observed sample that is not predicted by the best-fit model. Testing alternative models does not alleviate this tension; future population studies may mitigate this limitation by incorporating robust fluence and redshift measurements.
papers.comment: Submitted to ApJ

papers.t: Kinetic moment estimates and a one-sided Lyapunov barrier for the relativistic fermionic Michie-King equation
papers.abs: We study the cutoff Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR), or relativistic fermionic Michie--King, equation of state along an equilibrium family with fixed Tolman--Klein invariants. Three kinetic moments give exact formulas for both the pressure-to-density ratio and the derivative of pressure. Cauchy--Schwarz yields a global relation between these two quantities. It implies vertical vector-field domination of the associated Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff system by the linear equation of state $P=ρc^2/\sqrt3$ in the physical wedge $0<y\leq3x$. We construct a filled, one-sided version of the Bors--Stańczy Lyapunov barrier and check every boundary. This controls all outward excursions, including those after a lower exit from a Lyapunov sublevel. For regular configurations the resulting explicit Lambert bound is $2Gm(r)/(rc^2)<0.6879212521$. Using the diagonal where this ratio has a stationary value sharpens the bound to $0.6734385929$. The argument is conditional on a regular TOV configuration and does not require a separate finite-radius existence theorem. We also identify and correct a logarithmic coefficient in the previously used explicit linear-comparator formula.

papers.t: Fast Radio Bursts Co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 from 400 to 1530 MHz
papers.abs: We present a sample of $15$ fast radio bursts (FRBs) that were co-detected by the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA-110) and the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) between 2022 and 2024, of which $12$ have channelized voltage data from both instruments and 9 have secure redshifts. All but one are as-yet-non-repeating. Most bursts span the entire bandwidth of each instrument (400-800 MHz for CHIME, 1280-1530 MHz for DSA-110), significantly expanding the number of FRBs known to emit across $>1$ GHz of spectral bandwidth and constraining the spectral evolution of energy and propagation effects. On average, the FRBs exhibit higher spectral energies (up to a factor of $\sim10$) in the CHIME band but are lower in peak flux density due to substantial pulse broadening. The sample mean (median) spectral index $-0.4\pm0.4$ ($-0.3\pm0.4$) is shallower than previously reported spectral indices, likely a selection effect. A third of the sample shows evidence for a spectral turnover, comparable to that seen in GHz-peaked pulsar and magnetar spectra. Joint scintillation and pulse broadening constraints indicate that nearly all bursts encounter multiple scattering screens, with pulse broadening originating within their host galaxies. The co-detected bursts are among the most scattered in the CHIME/FRB sample, while being the narrowest in the DSA-110 sample, indicating that CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 select different subsets of the FRB population; the interplay between intrinsic burst width, scattering, and the FRB search time resolution creates a narrow window of sensitivity to co-detected FRBs, providing a blueprint for future ultra-wideband FRB surveys.
papers.comment: 28 pages, 15 figures, submitted (companion paper: "Spectropolarimetric properties of fast radio bursts co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110" by Pandhi et al.)

papers.t: Spectropolarimetric properties of fast radio bursts co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110
papers.abs: We present spectropolarimetric analysis of twelve fast radio bursts (FRBs) co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110, eleven of which are apparently non-repeating. We obtain broadband spectral coverage (400-1530 MHz) for these FRBs and constrain propagation effects in their polarized spectra. We observe two notable spectral features: (i) in three FRBs, we find decreasing linear polarization fraction with increasing frequency and, (ii) in seven FRBs, we find that the linear polarization fraction decreases with decreasing frequency. The former spectral signature is commonly observed in radio pulsars and is suggestive of magnetospheric emission, where either the mixing of orthogonally polarized modes or incoherent summing of unresolved burst components may cause depolarization at high frequencies. The latter is consistent with depolarization due to multipath propagation. We report the first statistically significant correlation (3.5-3.9$σ$) between the extent of depolarization and amplitude of Faraday rotation arising from FRB host galaxies, implying that the two effects likely arise in the same turbulent, magnetoionic environments around FRB sources. The prevalence of depolarization in our sample suggests that turbulent environments that have, thus far, been predominantly associated with some repeating FRBs, may also be commonly present around a subset of apparently non-repeating FRBs. We highlight a systematic bias for detecting a disproportionately high fraction of constant polarization angle (PA) profiles in low-frequency FRB surveys due to amplified scatter broadening, which we also observe in two of our co-detected FRBs.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 5 figures, submitted (companion paper: "Fast Radio Bursts Co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 from 400 to 1530 MHz" by S. K. Ocker & K. Nimmo et al.)

papers.t: Dual Horizon-MAD: A New Mode of Binary Black Hole Magnetically Arrested Accretion with Saturated Horizon Magnetic Fluxes and Intermittent Minidisks
papers.abs: Reliable first-principles predictions of multimessenger signals from inspiralling supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) require magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations in full general relativity (GR) that resolve the accretion flow down to the black hole horizons. However, performing such simulations long enough to relax the magnetohydrodynamics near the BBHs is computationally challenging and a source of uncertainty in modeling efforts. In this work, we present the longest MHD simulation of circumbinary disk (CBD) accretion onto a SMBBH in full GR. The equal-mass, quasicircular, nonspining BBH starts at an initial separation of $d/M=30$ and evolves over $\sim56$ orbits ($t \simeq 52,000 \, GM/c^3$), relaxing the magnetic field dynamics within the CBD cavity. After $\sim 23$ orbits and persistent magnetically arrested minidisks, the accretion enters a new magnetically arrested mode which we call dual horizon-MAD (DH-MAD). In DH-MAD, the dimensionless horizon magnetic fluxes remain saturated at $φ_{BH}\sim 20$ driving magnetic flux eruptions from the vicinity of the BH horizons, and the vertical magnetic flux in the cavity saturates, but no flux eruptions occur at the cavity-CBD boundary. During this DH-MAD phase, there is also a shift in the total mass accretion rate variability, which exhibits a periodicity of $f\sim 1.8 f_{\rm orb}$, while the accretion rate modulation on the individual black holes occurs almost at the orbital period, $f\sim 0.9 f_{\rm orb}$. $φ_{BH}$ also exhibits a robust periodicity at $f\sim 0.4 f_{\rm orb}$, suggesting that quasiperiodic nonthermal emission from magnetic reconnection near the horizons could be a smoking gun electromagnetic counterpart to inspiraling SMBBHs. Finally, minidisks around the BHs become intermittent in the DH-MAD phase, even at a separation of $d/M = 24$, likely due to the large plasma magnetization in the optically thin cavity.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 12 figures. Comments welcome!

papers.t: Scintillation arcs for fast pulsar binaries: the Double Pulsar
papers.abs: The double pulsar PSR J0737-3039A is a prime system for tests of gravity. A precise distance would strengthen these tests and also open up the possibility to measure the fast pulsar's moment of inertia, allowing a direct constraint on the equation of state of ultra-dense matter. Current parallax estimates from pulsar timing and very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) are in tension, which motivates complementary constraints. Information about distances is encoded in pulsar scintillation, but a complication for the double pulsar is that rapid orbital motion makes the interpretation difficult. We introduce an orbital motion ``resampling'' technique to overcome this complication, and use it to determine the properties of the principal scattering screen and the pulsar binary. Our fits yield a pulsar distance, of $781^{+62}_{-94}{\rm\,pc}$, in better agreement with the VLBI-based distance, but find that the nearly edge-on orbit precludes a precise measurement. For the principal screen, we infer a distance of $270^{+24}_{-23}{\rm\,pc}$, an orientation of $73.1^{\circ}\pm2.6^{\circ}$ E of N, and a transverse speed of $-15.2\pm1.0{\rm\,km/s}$. We also demonstrate the presence of a second screen, whose properties we can only partially determine: it is oriented roughly perpendicularly to the first screen and at a larger distance, of $\gtrsim\!547{\rm\,pc}$. To benchmark our technique and its uncertainties, we develop simulations of the system, generating artificial data that match the characteristics of the observed ones. We also discuss how future improvements to the method and use of the second screen could enable a more precise distance measurement.

papers.t: Higgs-portal dark matter beyond kinetic equilibrium
papers.abs: We revisit the scalar, vector, and fermion Higgs-portal dark matter models in the resonant regime without assuming kinetic equilibrium during the freeze-out. We compute the relic abundance by solving the full momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation and compare the results with the standard momentum-averaged treatment. We find that the standard treatment significantly underestimates the relic abundance below the resonance, apart from the fermionic case with a purely scalar portal coupling where the difference is negligible. The deviation from the standard treatment is largest for fermionic models with pseudoscalar interactions, corresponding to factor of 10 in terms of the coupling that reproduces the correct relic abundance. For the scalar and vector cases the corresponding difference is up to a factor of 2. We confront the resulting parameter space with the latest constraints from direct and indirect detection, as well as collider experiments. We find the full momentum-dependent results systematically strengthen the direct detection constraints.
papers.comment: 16 pages, 4 figures. Comments welcome

papers.t: Empirical Mass and Radius Relations for Main-sequence Stars from Detached Eclipsing Binaries
papers.abs: Detached eclipsing binaries have long served as fundamental calibrators for stellar models because they provide precise measurements of stellar masses and radii. Given a sample of detached eclipsing binaries, we can derive empirical relations between spectroscopic parameters (effective temperatures, surface gravities and abundances) and stellar masses and radii. We use a sample of 605 stars (330 with metallicities) in detached eclipsing binaries to update and refine these empirical models for main-sequence stars. An eight-term polynomial model reproduces the radii and masses of the eclipsing binary calibrators with an RMS scatter of $σ_{\log R} = 0.0161$ dex (3.8%) and $σ_{\log M} = 0.0322$ dex (7.7%), respectively. Most of this scatter is explained by the parameter uncertainties - the estimated intrinsic scatters in the radius and mass are only $σ_{\rm int}=0.0085$ and $0.017$ dex (2.0% and 4.0%). The predicted mass and radius of the Sun are $(1.028\pm0.004)\ M_\odot$ and $(1.014\pm0.002)\ R_\odot$. A 14-term model, while formally preferred, explains little more of the intrinsic scatter. We additionally provide the equivalent relations in terms of the mean stellar density instead of the surface gravity for use with exoplanet host stars. If we compare the 8-term model to MIST and PARSEC model stars with closely matched spectroscopic parameters, we find systematic differences. For example, the radii of hot (cool) stars are systematically over- (under-)estimated in both models by several percent.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 12 figures

papers.t: Long-Term Evolution of Hills-Captured Stars with TDE Disk Collisions: Links to Repeating Nuclear Transients
papers.abs: Quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) and repeating partial tidal disruption event (rpTDE) candidates are widely interpreted as being powered by a star on an hours-to-years orbit around a massive black hole (MBH). Every such orbiter model presupposes a star delivered onto an extraordinarily compact orbit without being destroyed, but it is unclear whether this is achievable. We follow the coupled orbital and stellar evolution of stars captured by the Hills mechanism, combining gas drag and per-collision mass loss from recurrent TDE disks with gravitational-wave (GW) orbital decay and stochastic two-body relaxation in a Monte Carlo model. Conventionally, the EMRI-formation criterion is based on comparing the timescales of GW decay and orbital angular momentum relaxation. We find that this criterion severely overestimates the EMRI rate: for relaxation timescales shorter than a Hubble time, most Hills-captured stars are tidally disrupted before GW emission can circularize the stellar orbit. Instead, TDE-disk drag plays a crucial role in the orbital evolution and can boost the fraction of stars reaching QPE orbits by an order of magnitude or more, assuming that the disk aspect ratio is relatively large $H/r \sim 0.1$. We also find that collisional ablation imposes a minimum orbital period that rises with MBH mass and precludes sub-day orbits for $M_{\rm BH} \gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$, unless GWs alone can drive orbital decay faster than orbital relaxation. This can explain the observed preference of short-period QPEs for low-mass MBHs. Most known rpTDEs lie below the Hills-capture period minimum and thus require additional orbital decay, which TDE-disk drag can plausibly supply. These results support the viability of the orbiter model; our predictions of the MBH mass and orbital period distributions can be used to further test this model.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 13 figures, 3 tables; to be submitted to The Open Journal of Astrophysics

papers.t: On the distribution function for cross-correlation estimators in cosmology and beyond
papers.abs: The ubiquitous Gaussian distribution, $e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2π}$, has mean of zero and variance of 1. It is well known that the estimator $\widehat{x^2} = N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N x_i^2$ for the variance obtained from $N$ samples $x_i$ is drawn from a $χ_n^2$ distribution, a result used often to assess the implications of data for a model. One often also needs to measure the covariance, or cross-correlation, of two different variables $x$ and $y$. If the distributions for $x$ and $y$ are both gaussian but independent of each other, the estimator $N^{-1}\sum_i x_i y_i$ for the cross-correlation is distributed about its expectation value (zero) with variance unity. The distribution function for this estimator may also be required to interpret data, for example in the measurement of cosmological cross-correlations. This distribution---the cross-correlation analog of the $χ_n^2$ distribution---appears in the literature, but it has not been widely internalized by many in the field. We therefore here present two pedagogical derivations of this distribution and discuss some of its properties. We discuss in particular the connection to cosmological observables, but note several other areas of physics where these results may apply.
papers.comment: 7 pages

papers.t: Resolved internal dynamics of a globular cluster candidate in a cosmological simulation at cosmic dawn
papers.abs: Globular clusters (GCs) are among the oldest and densest stellar systems in the Universe. Their compact sizes and old ages imply they must have assembled rapidly in the early Universe, yet the detailed physical mechanisms responsible for their formation remain uncertain. Although several scenarios have been proposed, cosmological simulations have so far been unable to resolve their detailed formation and internal dynamical structure at birth. Using a cosmological simulation that uniquely combines sub-parsec resolution with the formation of individual star particles, we follow the gravitational collapse and assembly of a compact stellar system with GC-progenitor mass and size, while directly resolving its internal dynamics and tracing the build-up of its angular momentum. The system assembles most of its stellar mass within 3 Myr, at $z\simeq10.5$, it rapidly becomes gas-poor, star-dominated, and develops ordered internal rotation acquired largely through the hierarchical assembly of distinct stellar subsystems. It forms as a satellite of a larger stellar complex within the virial radius of the $M_{\rm vir}\simeq1.73\times10^8\,M_\odot$ dark-matter halo hosting it. Its density, size and mass overlap with those of compact stellar systems recently observed by JWST at high redshift. These results indicate that GC progenitors can have well-defined internal kinematic structures already after their formation.
papers.comment: Accepted in principle for publication in Nature Astronomy (6/11/2026), 4 Figures, 5 Extended Data Figures

papers.t: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
papers.abs: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark-electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an annual-modulation search, for which the sensitivity scales as $S \lesssim \sqrt{B}$. Modern DAQs already record this rate, continuously in triggerless systems such as the XENONnT and PandaX-4T DAQs, and within trigger windows in LZ, so no new hardware is required. Using measured dark-electron rates, we estimate the sensitivity of XENONnT, LZ, PandaX-4T, PandaX-xT, and XLZD.
